subsystems.name: Optical sensing head
subsystems.role: shines light into the finger and measures what comes back, looking for glucose's faint spectral fingerprint.

subsystems.name: Skin-contact optics
subsystems.role: couples light into tissue reproducibly, despite the fact that every finger is different.

subsystems.name: Signal and chemometrics engine
subsystems.role: separates a glucose signal thousands of times weaker than the water, fat and protein around it.

subsystems.name: Motion and confounder sensing
subsystems.role: flags the many things that corrupt an optical reading.

subsystems.name: Physiology model
subsystems.role: converts a tissue measurement into a blood-glucose estimate.

subsystems.name: Power, radio and app
subsystems.role: fits computation and wireless into a ring, and shows trends and alerts.

buildSteps.title: Prove the physics in the lab
buildSteps.detail: Measure glucose in tissue phantoms, then in skin, against blood reference samples, to see whether the signal is detectable at safe light intensities. This is the step that has defeated most attempts.

buildSteps.title: Build the optical bench
buildSteps.detail: Assemble laser or LED, optics and detector on a rig and run glucose-clamp studies, where blood glucose is deliberately held at known levels while optical data is recorded.

buildSteps.title: Shrink it into a ring
buildSteps.detail: Miniaturise source, optics and detector, stabilise temperature, and design a skin interface that presses the same way on every wearer.

buildSteps.title: Train the calibration model
buildSteps.detail: Feed paired optical and blood-glucose data into a chemometric or machine-learning model, then test it on people who were not in the training set — the hardest test.

buildSteps.title: Combat confounders
buildSteps.detail: Correct for motion, perfusion changes, ambient light, skin tone, finger pressure and temperature, and decide how often a user must recalibrate.

buildSteps.title: Run clinical validation
buildSteps.detail: Measure accuracy against the accepted standards for glucose monitors, including performance in the low range where errors are dangerous, and report a mean absolute relative difference figure.

buildSteps.title: Clear regulation
buildSteps.detail: Seek medical-device clearance, and demonstrate that laser or light exposure stays within eye and skin safety limits.

buildSteps.title: Scale manufacture
buildSteps.detail: Make thousands of units with sensor-to-sensor consistency, in biocompatible materials that survive sweat, soap and daily wear.

buildSteps.title: Monitor after launch
buildSteps.detail: Track drift, recalibration frequency and any harms, since a plausible-but-wrong reading can lead to a wrong insulin dose.

prerequisites.why: laboratory Raman and near-infrared instruments work, but shrinking the light path into a ring while keeping signal quality is unsolved.
statistical methods exist, but they need large sets of accurately paired optical and blood data that nobody has yet collected at scale.
fingerstick and existing sensor-based monitors provide the labels any model must be trained and judged against.
the relationship and time lag between tissue and blood glucose is understood in outline but varies between people and conditions.
optical readings are known to vary with skin pigmentation and blood flow, and no validated correction exists for glucose sensing.

pathway.milestone: smart rings measure pulse, temperature and sleep, and some market vague 'metabolic' scores, while fingerstick and implantable or wearable enzymatic sensors remain the only accurate glucose route
pathway.unlocks: a form factor people will actually wear, waiting for a sensor that works.

pathway.milestone: research-grade Raman or near-infrared devices reach usable accuracy in supervised studies with daily calibration
pathway.unlocks: non-invasive trend tracking, with confirmatory fingersticks before any treatment decision.

pathway.milestone: hybrid systems pair a non-invasive optical sensor with an occasional minimally invasive element for re-calibration
pathway.unlocks: fewer needle events per week while keeping clinical accuracy.

pathway.milestone: a ring-grade sensor that stays accurate for months without calibration and passes the standards required for dosing decisions
pathway.unlocks: needle-free monitoring for the hundreds of millions of people with diabetes and for general metabolic health.
